sections.title: What Is Reranking?
sections.body:
> **Reranking is a second-pass scoring step that takes an initial set of retrieved documents and re-orders them by TRUE relevance to the query — going far beyond simple vector similarity.**
> It is the single highest-impact improvement you can make to a RAG system.

sections.title: The Core Problem — Why Vector Search Alone Fails
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│         WHY VECTOR SIMILARITY ≠ TRUE RELEVANCE                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  VECTOR SEARCH (what basic RAG does):
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Query:  "What causes memory leaks in Python?"

  Step 1: Embed query → vector [0.23, 0.71, 0.44, ...]
  Step 2: Find documents with similar vectors
  Step 3: Return top-K by cosine similarity

  Results ranked by EMBEDDING SIMILARITY:
  ┌────┬─────────────────────────────────────────┬───────────┐
  │ #1 │ "Python memory management overview"     │ sim=0.89  │
  │ #2 │ "Memory allocation in Python runtime"   │ sim=0.87  │
  │ #3 │ "Python garbage collection basics"      │ sim=0.85  │
  │ #4 │ "How to find and fix memory leaks"      │ sim=0.83  │
  │ #5 │ "Python performance optimization tips"  │ sim=0.81  │
  └────┴─────────────────────────────────────────┴───────────┘

  THE PROBLEM:
  Doc #4 DIRECTLY ANSWERS the question ("find and fix memory leaks")
  but is ranked #4 because its EMBEDDING doesn't perfectly align.

  Docs #1, #2, #3 are RELATED but don't actually answer the question.
  They get high similarity scores because they share many vocabulary
  words with the query.

  VECTOR SIMILARITY measures:         RERANKING measures:
  ───────────────────────────         ───────────────────────────
  "Are these embeddings close?"       "Does this doc ANSWER the query?"
  Topic overlap                       Actual relevance
  Vocabulary similarity               Semantic intent match
  Fast (ANN search)                   Slower (cross-attention)
  Approximate                         Precise

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  AFTER RERANKING:
  ┌────┬─────────────────────────────────────────┬───────────┐
  │ #1 │ "How to find and fix memory leaks"      │ score=0.97│ ←MOVED UP
  │ #2 │ "Python garbage collection basics"      │ score=0.82│
  │ #3 │ "Python memory management overview"     │ score=0.76│
  │ #4 │ "Memory allocation in Python runtime"   │ score=0.71│
  │ #5 │ "Python performance optimization tips"  │ score=0.58│
  └────┴─────────────────────────────────────────┴───────────┘

  The RIGHT document is now #1. Answer quality: dramatically better.
```

sections.title: How Each Approach Works
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│         BI-ENCODER (Vector Search) vs CROSS-ENCODER (Reranker)  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  BI-ENCODER (what vector DBs use):
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  Query  → [Encoder] → Vector Q
  Doc 1  → [Encoder] → Vector D1    similarity(Q, D1) = 0.89
  Doc 2  → [Encoder] → Vector D2    similarity(Q, D2) = 0.87
  Doc 3  → [Encoder] → Vector D3    similarity(Q, D3) = 0.85

  Query and documents are encoded SEPARATELY.
  Similarity = dot product / cosine of independent vectors.
  FAST (pre-compute doc vectors) but APPROXIMATE.

  CROSS-ENCODER (what rerankers use):
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  [Query + Doc 1 concatenated] → [Cross-Encoder] → Score: 0.97
  [Query + Doc 2 concatenated] → [Cross-Encoder] → Score: 0.82
  [Query + Doc 3 concatenated] → [Cross-Encoder] → Score: 0.76

  Query and document are encoded TOGETHER.
  The model can attend to RELATIONSHIPS between query words
  and document words — much deeper understanding.
  SLOWER (can't pre-compute) but FAR MORE ACCURATE.

  WHY CROSS-ENCODER IS MORE ACCURATE:
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  Query: "What causes Python memory leaks?"

  Bi-encoder sees:
  "Python memory leaks" ←→ "Python memory management"
  These embed similarly → high score BUT not the answer

  Cross-encoder sees:
  "What CAUSES Python memory leaks?"
  + "Python memory management is about how Python allocates..."
  → Understands: "allocates" ≠ "causes leaks"
  → Scores lower ✅

  Cross-encoder sees:
  "What CAUSES Python memory leaks?"
  + "Memory leaks are CAUSED BY circular references, large objects..."
  → Understands: "caused by" directly answers "causes"
  → Scores higher ✅
```

sections.title: The Two-Stage Retrieval Pipeline
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│            THE GOLD STANDARD: TWO-STAGE PIPELINE                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  STAGE 1: RECALL (cast wide net — be exhaustive)
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Goal: Find ALL potentially relevant documents.
  Speed: Fast (vector search, ANN algorithms).
  Quality: Approximate (good enough to shortlist).
  Retrieve: Top 50-100 candidates.

  STAGE 2: PRECISION (pick the best — be selective)
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Goal: Find the BEST documents from the candidates.
  Speed: Slower (cross-encoder, runs on 50-100 docs).
  Quality: High precision.
  Return: Top 3-5 for LLM context.

  THE FULL PIPELINE:
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  User Query
       │
       ▼
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  STAGE 1: VECTOR SEARCH                                │
  │  Query → Embed → Search 10M docs → Top 50 candidates  │
  │  Time: ~20ms                                           │
  └────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘
                           │ 50 candidate docs
                           ▼
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  STAGE 2: RERANKER                                     │
  │  Score each of 50 docs vs query → Rerank → Top 5      │
  │  Time: ~150ms                                          │
  └────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘
                           │ 5 highly relevant docs
                           ▼
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  STAGE 3: LLM GENERATION                              │
  │  5 docs injected as context → Generate answer          │
  │  Time: ~800ms                                          │
  └────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘
                           │
                           ▼
                    High-quality answer ✅

  TOTAL: ~970ms vs 820ms without reranking.
  150ms extra → dramatically better answers.

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  WHY NOT JUST RERANK EVERYTHING?

  10,000,000 docs × cross-encoder = HOURS
  50 candidates × cross-encoder   = 150ms ✅

  Vector search is the "cheap filter".
  Reranker is the "expensive precision scorer".
  Use them together, not one or the other.
```

sections.title: Reranking Metrics — How to Measure Improvement
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│            MEASURING RERANKING IMPROVEMENT                      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  METRIC 1: MRR (Mean Reciprocal Rank)
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  How high is the FIRST relevant result on average?

  MRR = average of (1 / rank_of_first_relevant_doc)

  Without reranking:  relevant doc at rank 4 → 1/4 = 0.25
  After reranking:    relevant doc at rank 1 → 1/1 = 1.00

  Higher MRR = relevant doc appears earlier = better answers.

  METRIC 2: NDCG@K (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain)
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  How well are the TOP-K documents ranked by relevance?
  Documents ranked higher contribute MORE to the score.

  NDCG@5 = 0.72 before reranking
  NDCG@5 = 0.91 after reranking
  ↑ 26% improvement in top-5 ranking quality

  METRIC 3: RECALL@K
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  What % of relevant docs appear in the top-K results?

  Before reranking:  Recall@5 = 0.60 (3/5 relevant in top-5)
  After reranking:   Recall@5 = 0.80 (4/5 relevant in top-5)

  METRIC 4: ANSWER QUALITY (end-to-end)
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  The ultimate metric: Does the final answer improve?

  Test: 100 questions with known correct answers.
  Without reranking:  68% correct answers
  With reranking:     84% correct answers
  ↑ 24% improvement in answer accuracy
```

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- RERANKING BASE — Shared interfaces and utilities.
- A document with optional relevance metadata.
- Result from a reranker call.
- Print before/after comparison.
- Assign scores and sort
- Build scored docs in new order
- Convert to 0-indexed, validate
- Score = 1.0 for rank 1, decreasing

**Defines:** `Document`, `RerankerResult`, `RerankerBase`, `CrossEncoderReranker`, `CohereReranker`, `LLMReranker`, `RRFReranker`, `HybridReranker`, `TwoStageRAG`

```python name=reranking/reranker_base.py
"""
RERANKING BASE — Shared interfaces and utilities.
All reranker implementations inherit from RerankerBase.
"""
import time
from abc         import ABC, abstractmethod
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing      import Optional

@dataclass
class Document:
    """A document with optional relevance metadata."""
    id:             str
    content:        str
    title:          str          = ""
    source:         str          = ""
    vector_score:   float        = 0.0    # Original retrieval score
    rerank_score:   float        = 0.0    # After reranking
    original_rank:  int          = 0
    final_rank:     int          = 0
    metadata:       dict         = field(default_factory=dict)

    def __repr__(self):
        return (
            f"Doc(rank={self.final_rank}, "
            f"rerank={self.rerank_score:.3f}, "
            f"title='{self.title[:40]}')"
        )

@dataclass
class RerankerResult:
    """Result from a reranker call."""
    query:            str
    reranked_docs:    list[Document]
    original_docs:    list[Document]
    latency_ms:       float
    model_used:       str
    rank_changes:     list[dict]    = field(default_factory=list)

    def top_k(self, k: int = 5) -> list[Document]:
        return self.reranked_docs[:k]

    def print_comparison(self, top_k: int = 5):
        """Print before/after comparison."""
        print(f"\n  📊 Reranking Comparison (top {top_k}):")
        print(f"  Query: '{self.query[:60]}'")
        print(f"  {'─'*70}")
        print(f"  {'BEFORE':^35} │ {'AFTER':^35}")
        print(f"  {'─'*70}")

        orig  = self.original_docs[:top_k]
        after = self.reranked_docs[:top_k]

        for i in range(max(len(orig), len(after))):
            o_doc = orig[i]  if i < len(orig)  else None
            a_doc = after[i] if i < len(after) else None

            o_str = (f"#{i+1} [{o_doc.vector_score:.3f}] "
                     f"{o_doc.title[:25]}") if o_doc else ""
            a_str = (f"#{i+1} [{a_doc.rerank_score:.3f}] "
                     f"{a_doc.title[:25]}") if a_doc else ""

            # Mark rank changes
            moved = ""
            if o_doc and a_doc and o_doc.id != a_doc.id:
                moved = " ↔"

            print(f"  {o_str:35s} │ {a_str:35s}{moved}")

        print(f"  {'─'*70}")
        print(f"  Reranker: {self.model_used} | "
              f"Latency: {self.latency_ms:.0f}ms")

class RerankerBase(ABC):
    """Abstract base class for all rerankers."""

    @abstractmethod
    def rerank(
        self,
        query:    str,
        docs:     list[Document],
        top_k:    int = 5,
    ) -> RerankerResult:
        """
        Rerank documents by relevance to query.
        Returns top_k most relevant documents, reordered.
        """
        pass

    def _build_result(
        self,
        query:         str,
        original_docs: list[Document],
        scored_docs:   list[Document],
        top_k:         int,
        model:         str,
        latency_ms:    float,
    ) -> RerankerResult:
        """Build standardized result object."""
        # Assign final ranks
        for i, doc in enumerate(scored_docs):
            doc.final_rank = i + 1

        # Track rank changes
        rank_changes = []
        for doc in scored_docs[:top_k]:
            orig_rank = next(
                (d.original_rank for d in original_docs
                 if d.id == doc.id), 0
            )
            change = orig_rank - doc.final_rank
            if change != 0:
                rank_changes.append({
                    "doc_id":     doc.id,
                    "title":      doc.title[:40],
                    "moved_from": orig_rank,
                    "moved_to":   doc.final_rank,
                    "delta":      change,
                })

        return RerankerResult(
            query         = query,
            reranked_docs = scored_docs,
            original_docs = original_docs,
            latency_ms    = latency_ms,
            model_used    = model,
            rank_changes  = rank_changes,
        )
```

```python name=reranking/cross_encoder_reranker.py
"""
CROSS-ENCODER RERANKER
Uses sentence-transformers cross-encoder for precise reranking.
The gold standard for offline/local reranking.
"""
import time
from reranking.reranker_base import (
    Document, RerankerBase, RerankerResult
)

class CrossEncoderReranker(RerankerBase):
    """
    Cross-Encoder Reranker using sentence-transformers.

    How it works:
    1. Concatenate [query, document] for each doc
    2. Pass through cross-encoder (BERT-based)
    3. Get relevance score for each pair
    4. Sort by score

    Models (ordered by quality vs speed):
    ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2    → Fast,  good quality   (6 layers)
    ms-marco-MiniLM-L-12-v2   → Balanced              (12 layers)
    ms-marco-electra-base      → Best quality, slower
    bge-reranker-base          → Great for multilingual
    bge-reranker-large         → Best quality overall
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        model_name: str = "cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2",
    ):
        self.model_name = model_name
        self._model     = None    # Lazy load

    def _load_model(self):
        """Lazy-load the model (expensive to load)."""
        if self._model is None:
            try:
                from sentence_transformers import CrossEncoder
                print(f"  📥 Loading cross-encoder: {self.model_name}")
                self._model = CrossEncoder(self.model_name)
                print(f"  ✅ Cross-encoder loaded")
            except ImportError:
                raise ImportError(
                    "Install: pip install sentence-transformers"
                )
        return self._model

    def rerank(
        self,
        query:  str,
        docs:   list[Document],
        top_k:  int = 5,
    ) -> RerankerResult:
        """
        Rerank documents using cross-encoder.
        """
        if not docs:
            return RerankerResult(
                query         = query,
                reranked_docs = [],
                original_docs = [],
                latency_ms    = 0,
                model_used    = self.model_name,
            )

        start = time.time()
        model = self._load_model()

        # Assign original ranks
        originals = []
        for i, doc in enumerate(docs):
            d = Document(**{
                k: v for k, v in doc.__dict__.items()
            })
            d.original_rank = i + 1
            originals.append(d)

        # Build query-document pairs
        pairs = [(query, doc.content) for doc in originals]

        # Score all pairs
        scores = model.predict(pairs)

        # Assign scores and sort
        scored_docs = []
        for doc, score in zip(originals, scores):
            d              = Document(**{k: v for k, v in doc.__dict__.items()})
            d.rerank_score = float(score)
            scored_docs.append(d)

        scored_docs.sort(key=lambda x: x.rerank_score, reverse=True)

        latency = (time.time() - start) * 1000
        print(f"  ✅ Cross-Encoder reranked {len(docs)} docs "
              f"→ top {top_k} in {latency:.0f}ms")

        return self._build_result(
            query         = query,
            original_docs = originals,
            scored_docs   = scored_docs[:top_k],
            top_k         = top_k,
            model         = self.model_name,
            latency_ms    = latency,
        )
```

```python name=reranking/cohere_reranker.py
"""
COHERE RERANKER
Uses Cohere's Rerank API — best-in-class production reranker.
No model to host. Just API calls.
"""
import os, time
from reranking.reranker_base import (
    Document, RerankerBase, RerankerResult
)

class CohereReranker(RerankerBase):
    """
    Cohere Rerank API reranker.

    Why Cohere Rerank?
    ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    ✅ No model to download or host
    ✅ Best-in-class relevance scores
    ✅ Handles long documents (up to 512 tokens per chunk)
    ✅ Multilingual support
    ✅ Simple REST API
    ✅ Used in production by major AI companies

    Models:
    ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    rerank-english-v3.0    → Best for English content
    rerank-multilingual-v3.0 → 100+ languages
    rerank-english-v2.0    → Faster, slightly less accurate

    Pricing (2024): ~$0.001 per search unit (1 query + 1 doc)
    100 docs × $0.001 = $0.10 per reranking call
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        model: str = "rerank-english-v3.0",
        api_key: str = None,
    ):
        self.model   = model
        self.api_key = api_key or os.getenv("COHERE_API_KEY")
        self._client = None

    def _get_client(self):
        if self._client is None:
            try:
                import cohere
                self._client = cohere.Client(self.api_key)
            except ImportError:
                raise ImportError("Install: pip install cohere")
        return self._client

    def rerank(
        self,
        query:  str,
        docs:   list[Document],
        top_k:  int = 5,
    ) -> RerankerResult:
        """Rerank using Cohere API."""
        if not docs:
            return RerankerResult(
                query=query, reranked_docs=[],
                original_docs=[], latency_ms=0,
                model_used=self.model,
            )

        start  = time.time()
        client = self._get_client()

        # Assign original ranks
        originals = []
        for i, doc in enumerate(docs):
            d = Document(**{k: v for k, v in doc.__dict__.items()})
            d.original_rank = i + 1
            originals.append(d)

        # Call Cohere API
        response = client.rerank(
            model     = self.model,
            query     = query,
            documents = [d.content for d in originals],
            top_n     = min(top_k, len(originals)),
        )

        # Build scored docs in new order
        scored_docs = []
        for result in response.results:
            doc = Document(
                **{k: v for k, v in originals[result.index].__dict__.items()}
            )
            doc.rerank_score = result.relevance_score
            scored_docs.append(doc)

        latency = (time.time() - start) * 1000
        print(f"  ✅ Cohere reranked {len(docs)} docs "
              f"→ top {top_k} in {latency:.0f}ms")

        return self._build_result(
            query         = query,
            original_docs = originals,
            scored_docs   = scored_docs,
            top_k         = top_k,
            model         = self.model,
            latency_ms    = latency,
        )
```

```python name=reranking/llm_reranker.py
"""
LLM RERANKER
Uses GPT-4o to score document relevance.
Highest quality. Best for complex queries.
"""
import os, re, json, time, asyncio
from openai import AzureOpenAI
from dotenv import load_dotenv
from reranking.reranker_base import (
    Document, RerankerBase, RerankerResult
)

load_dotenv()
client = AzureOpenAI(
    azure_endpoint = os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT"),
    api_key        = os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY"),
    api_version    = os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION"),
)
MODEL = os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT")

class LLMReranker(RerankerBase):
    """
    LLM-based reranker.

    Uses the LLM itself to judge document relevance.
    Most expensive but highest quality — especially for
    nuanced, domain-specific, or multi-part questions.

    Two modes:
    ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    POINTWISE: Score each doc independently (0-10)
               Pros: Simple, parallelizable
               Cons: Scores not comparable across docs

    LISTWISE:  Show all docs at once, get ranked list
               Pros: Relative ranking, best quality
               Cons: Context window limits (max ~20 docs)
    """

    def __init__(self, mode: str = "listwise"):
        assert mode in ("pointwise", "listwise")
        self.mode = mode

    def _score_pointwise(
        self,
        query:  str,
        doc:    Document,
    ) -> float:
        """Score one document against query (0-10)."""
        raw = client.chat.completions.create(
            model    = MODEL,
            messages = [
                {
                    "role":    "system",
                    "content": """You are a relevance judge.
Score how well this document answers the query.

Return ONLY valid JSON:
{"score": 0-10, "reason": "one sentence"}

Scoring guide:
10 = Directly and completely answers the query
8-9 = Very relevant, answers most of the query
6-7 = Somewhat relevant, partial answer
4-5 = Related topic but doesn't answer the query
1-3 = Tangentially related
0   = Completely irrelevant""",
                },
                {
                    "role":    "user",
                    "content": (
                        f"Query: {query}\n\n"
                        f"Document:\n{doc.content[:600]}"
                    ),
                },
            ],
            temperature = 0.0,
            max_tokens  = 80,
        ).choices[0].message.content or "{}"

        try:
            match = re.search(r'\{.*\}', raw, re.DOTALL)
            data  = json.loads(match.group()) if match else {}
            return float(data.get("score", 5)) / 10.0
        except Exception:
            return 0.5

    def _rank_listwise(
        self,
        query: str,
        docs:  list[Document],
    ) -> list[int]:
        """
        Rank all documents at once.
        Returns list of original indices in ranked order.
        """
        doc_list = "\n\n".join([
            f"[DOC {i+1}]: {doc.title}\n{doc.content[:300]}"
            for i, doc in enumerate(docs)
        ])

        raw = client.chat.completions.create(
            model    = MODEL,
            messages = [
                {
                    "role":    "system",
                    "content": """Rank these documents by relevance to the query.
Most relevant first.

Return ONLY a JSON array of document numbers (1-indexed):
[3, 1, 5, 2, 4]
(meaning doc 3 is most relevant, then doc 1, etc.)""",
                },
                {
                    "role":    "user",
                    "content": (
                        f"Query: {query}\n\n"
                        f"Documents:\n{doc_list}"
                    ),
                },
            ],
            temperature = 0.0,
            max_tokens  = 100,
        ).choices[0].message.content or "[]"

        try:
            match = re.search(r'\[.*\]', raw, re.DOTALL)
            ranks = json.loads(match.group()) if match else []
            # Convert to 0-indexed, validate
            return [
                r - 1 for r in ranks
                if isinstance(r, int) and 1 <= r <= len(docs)
            ]
        except Exception:
            return list(range(len(docs)))

    def rerank(
        self,
        query:  str,
        docs:   list[Document],
        top_k:  int = 5,
    ) -> RerankerResult:
        """Rerank using LLM."""
        if not docs:
            return RerankerResult(
                query=query, reranked_docs=[],
                original_docs=[], latency_ms=0,
                model_used=f"llm_{self.mode}",
            )

        start = time.time()

        # Assign original ranks
        originals = []
        for i, doc in enumerate(docs):
            d = Document(**{k: v for k, v in doc.__dict__.items()})
            d.original_rank = i + 1
            originals.append(d)

        if self.mode == "listwise":
            print(f"  🤖 LLM listwise reranking {len(docs)} docs...")
            ranked_indices = self._rank_listwise(query, originals)

            scored_docs = []
            for rank, idx in enumerate(ranked_indices):
                if 0 <= idx < len(originals):
                    d = Document(**{k: v for k, v in originals[idx].__dict__.items()})
                    # Score = 1.0 for rank 1, decreasing
                    d.rerank_score = 1.0 - (rank * 0.1)
                    scored_docs.append(d)

            # Add any docs not in ranked list
            ranked_ids = {originals[i].id for i in ranked_indices if 0 <= i < len(originals)}
            for doc in originals:
                if doc.id not in ranked_ids:
                    d = Document(**{k: v for k, v in doc.__dict__.items()})
                    d.rerank_score = 0.1
                    scored_docs.append(d)

        else:  # pointwise — score each independently
            print(f"  🤖 LLM pointwise scoring {len(docs)} docs...")
            scored_docs = []
            for doc in originals:
                score = self._score_pointwise(query, doc)
                d     = Document(**{k: v for k, v in doc.__dict__.items()})
                d.rerank_score = score
                scored_docs.append(d)
            scored_docs.sort(key=lambda x: x.rerank_score, reverse=True)

        latency = (time.time() - start) * 1000
        print(f"  ✅ LLM reranked {len(docs)} docs in {latency:.0f}ms")

        return self._build_result(
            query         = query,
            original_docs = originals,
            scored_docs   = scored_docs[:top_k],
            top_k         = top_k,
            model         = f"llm_{self.mode}_{MODEL}",
            latency_ms    = latency,
        )

"""
RECIPROCAL RANK FUSION (RRF)
Combines multiple ranked lists without a model.
Fast, robust, no API cost.
"""
import time
from reranking.reranker_base import (
    Document, RerankerBase, RerankerResult
)

class RRFReranker:
    """
    Reciprocal Rank Fusion.

    Combines multiple different retrieval result lists
    into one unified ranking.

    Formula:
    RRF_score(doc) = Σ 1 / (k + rank_in_list_i)
    where k = 60 (smoothing constant)

    Why k=60?
    ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Empirically found to work best across many benchmarks.
    Too small: top-ranked docs dominate too much.
    Too large: all positions treated equally (loses signal).

    Use Cases:
    ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    ✅ Combining BM25 + vector search results
    ✅ Combining results from multiple queries (Fusion RAG)
    ✅ Combining results from multiple models
    ✅ Ensemble of different retrieval strategies
    ✅ No API cost — pure computation
    """

    def __init__(self, k: int = 60):
        self.k = k

    def fuse(
        self,
        ranked_lists:  list[list[Document]],
        top_k:         int = 5,
        list_names:    list[str] = None,
    ) -> RerankerResult:
        """
        Fuse multiple ranked lists using RRF.

        ranked_lists: Each list is docs ranked by ONE retrieval method.
        top_k:        Number of top docs to return.
        list_names:   Optional names for each list (for display).
        """
        if not ranked_lists:
            return RerankerResult(
                query="", reranked_docs=[], original_docs=[],
                latency_ms=0, model_used="rrf",
            )

        start      = time.time()
        rrf_scores: dict[str, float] = {}
        doc_map:    dict[str, Document] = {}
        appearances:dict[str, int]   = {}

        # Collect all unique docs and compute RRF scores
        for list_idx, doc_list in enumerate(ranked_lists):
            list_name = (list_names[list_idx]
                         if list_names and list_idx < len(list_names)
                         else f"list_{list_idx}")

            for rank, doc in enumerate(doc_list, start=1):
                doc_id = doc.id

                # Store doc (first time seen)
                if doc_id not in doc_map:
                    doc_map[doc_id]     = doc
                    rrf_scores[doc_id]  = 0.0
                    appearances[doc_id] = 0

                # Add RRF score for this list
                rrf_scores[doc_id]  += 1.0 / (self.k + rank)
                appearances[doc_id] += 1

        # Sort by RRF score
        sorted_ids = sorted(
            rrf_scores.keys(),
            key=lambda did: rrf_scores[did],
            reverse=True,
        )

        # Build result documents
        scored_docs = []
        for rank, doc_id in enumerate(sorted_ids[:top_k], start=1):
            doc              = doc_map[doc_id]
            d                = Document(**{k: v for k, v in doc.__dict__.items()})
            d.rerank_score   = round(rrf_scores[doc_id], 6)
            d.final_rank     = rank
            d.metadata["rrf_appearances"] = appearances[doc_id]
            d.metadata["rrf_score"]       = d.rerank_score
            scored_docs.append(d)

        # Collect all original docs for reference
        all_originals = []
        for doc_list in ranked_lists:
            all_originals.extend(doc_list)

        latency = (time.time() - start) * 1000
        print(f"\n  ✅ RRF fused {len(ranked_lists)} lists "
              f"({sum(len(l) for l in ranked_lists)} total docs) "
              f"→ top {top_k} in {latency:.1f}ms")

        # Show fusion stats
        for i, doc in enumerate(scored_docs[:top_k], 1):
            appear = doc.metadata.get("rrf_appearances", 0)
            total  = len(ranked_lists)
            print(f"  #{i} [{doc.rerank_score:.5f}] "
                  f"appeared in {appear}/{total} lists: "
                  f"{doc.title[:35]}")

        return RerankerResult(
            query         = "",
            reranked_docs = scored_docs,
            original_docs = all_originals,
            latency_ms    = latency,
            model_used    = f"rrf_k{self.k}",
        )

class HybridReranker:
    """
    Hybrid Search + RRF Reranker.

    Combines:
    1. Vector search results (semantic similarity)
    2. BM25/keyword search results (exact matches)

    Then applies RRF to fuse the two ranked lists.

    This is the industry standard for production RAG:
    ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Vector search: great for semantic, meaning-based queries
    BM25:          great for exact names, codes, acronyms
    RRF fusion:    gets the best of both worlds

    Example:
    Query: "GPT-4o context window size"
    Vector: finds docs about "model capabilities" ← semantic
    BM25:   finds docs containing "GPT-4o" ← exact match
    RRF:    top result = doc with both "GPT-4o" AND context info ✅
    """

    def __init__(self, rrf_k: int = 60):
        self.rrf = RRFReranker(k=rrf_k)

    def _bm25_search(
        self,
        query: str,
        docs:  list[Document],
        top_k: int = 20,
    ) -> list[Document]:
        """
        BM25 keyword search.
        In production: use Elasticsearch, Opensearch, or rank_bm25.
        Here: simplified TF-IDF approximation.
        """
        import math

        query_terms = set(query.lower().split())
        scores = []

        for doc in docs:
            doc_words  = doc.content.lower().split()
            doc_len    = len(doc_words)
            avg_len    = 100  # Assumed average

            # BM25 score (simplified)
            k1, b     = 1.5, 0.75
            bm25_score = 0.0

            for term in query_terms:
                tf  = doc_words.count(term)
                idf = math.log(
                    (len(docs) + 1) / (1 + sum(
                        1 for d in docs if term in d.content.lower()
                    ))
                )
                tf_norm     = (tf * (k1 + 1)) / (
                    tf + k1 * (1 - b + b * doc_len / avg_len)
                )
                bm25_score += idf * tf_norm

            if bm25_score > 0:
                d              = Document(**{k: v for k, v in doc.__dict__.items()})
                d.vector_score = bm25_score
                scores.append(d)

        scores.sort(key=lambda x: x.vector_score, reverse=True)
        return scores[:top_k]

    def rerank(
        self,
        query:          str,
        vector_results: list[Document],
        all_docs:       list[Document] = None,
        top_k:          int = 5,
    ) -> RerankerResult:
        """
        Hybrid reranking: vector + BM25 + RRF fusion.
        """
        print(f"\n  🔀 Hybrid Search + RRF:")
        print(f"  Query: '{query[:55]}'")

        # BM25 on same doc pool
        docs_for_bm25  = all_docs or vector_results
        bm25_results   = self._bm25_search(
            query, docs_for_bm25, top_k=20
        )

        print(f"  Vector results: {len(vector_results)} docs")
        print(f"  BM25 results:   {len(bm25_results)} docs")

        # Fuse with RRF
        result = self.rrf.fuse(
            ranked_lists = [vector_results, bm25_results],
            top_k        = top_k,
            list_names   = ["vector_search", "bm25"],
        )
        result.query = query
        return result
```

RAW_DOCS = [

class TwoStageRAG:
    """
    Complete two-stage RAG pipeline with reranking.

    Stage 1: Vector search → Top 20 candidates
    Stage 2: Reranker      → Top 5 best docs
    Stage 3: LLM           → Generate answer
    """

    def __init__(self, reranker=None):
        self.reranker = reranker
        self._docs    = None
        self._build_index()

    def _embed(self, texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
        r = client.embeddings.create(
            input=[t.replace("\n", " ") for t in texts],
            model=EMBED_MODEL,
        )
        return [item.embedding for item in r.data]

    def _cosine(self, a, b) -> float:
        va = np.array(a, dtype=np.float32)
        vb = np.array(b, dtype=np.float32)
        return float(
            np.dot(va, vb) / (np.linalg.norm(va) * np.linalg.norm(vb) + 1e-10)
        )

    def _build_index(self):
        """Embed all documents."""
        print("  📚 Building document index...")
        texts = [d["content"] for d in RAW_DOCS]
        embs  = self._embed(texts)

        self._docs = []
        for raw, emb in zip(RAW_DOCS, embs):
            self._docs.append({**raw, "embedding": emb})
        print(f"  ✅ Indexed {len(self._docs)} docs")

    def _vector_search(
        self,
        query:  str,
        top_k:  int = 20,
    ) -> list[Document]:
        """Stage 1: Fast vector search to get candidates."""
        q_emb  = self._embed([query])[0]
        scored = []

        for doc in self._docs:
            score = self._cosine(q_emb, doc["embedding"])
            scored.append(Document(
                id           = doc["id"],
                title        = doc["title"],
                content      = doc["content"],
                vector_score = round(score, 4),
            ))

        scored.sort(key=lambda x: x.vector_score, reverse=True)

        # Assign original ranks
        for i, doc in enumerate(scored):
            doc.original_rank = i + 1

        return scored[:top_k]

    def _generate_answer(
        self,
        query:   str,
        docs:    list[Document],
    ) -> str:
        """Stage 3: Generate answer from top docs."""
        context = "\n\n".join([
            f"[{i+1}] {doc.title}:\n{doc.content}"
            for i, doc in enumerate(docs[:5])
        ])

        r = client.chat.completions.create(
            model    = MODEL,
            messages = [
                {
                    "role":    "system",
                    "content": "Answer based on the provided context. "
                               "Be specific and accurate.",
                },
                {
                    "role":    "user",
                    "content": f"Context:\n{context}\n\nQuestion: {query}",
                },
            ],
            temperature = 0.0,
            max_tokens  = 300,
        )
        return r.choices[0].message.content or ""

    def query(
        self,
        question:     str,
        show_details: bool = True,
    ) -> str:
        """
        Full two-stage RAG query.
        """
        print(f"\n{'═'*60}")
        print(f"🔍 TWO-STAGE RAG | Query: {question}")
        print(f"{'═'*60}")

        total_start = time.time()

        # ── Stage 1: Vector Search ─────────────────────
        print(f"\n  Stage 1: Vector Search → 20 candidates")
        stage1_start = time.time()
        candidates   = self._vector_search(question, top_k=20)
        stage1_ms    = (time.time() - stage1_start) * 1000

        if show_details:
            print(f"  Top 5 by vector score:")
            for doc in candidates[:5]:
                print(f"    #{doc.original_rank} "
                      f"[{doc.vector_score:.3f}] {doc.title}")

        # ── Stage 2: Reranking ─────────────────────────
        top_docs = candidates[:5]   # Default if no reranker

        if self.reranker:
            print(f"\n  Stage 2: Reranking...")
            result   = self.reranker.rerank(
                query = question,
                docs  = candidates,
                top_k = 5,
            )
            top_docs = result.top_k(5)

            if show_details:
                result.print_comparison(top_k=5)
        else:
            print(f"\n  Stage 2: No reranker (using vector top-5)")

        # ── Stage 3: Generate ──────────────────────────
        print(f"\n  Stage 3: Generating answer...")
        answer     = self._generate_answer(question, top_docs)
        total_ms   = (time.time() - total_start) * 1000

        print(f"\n  ✅ Answer: {answer}")
        print(f"\n  ⏱️  Timing: "
              f"Vector={stage1_ms:.0f}ms + "
              f"Rerank={total_ms-stage1_ms:.0f}ms + "
              f"Gen=~800ms | Total={total_ms:.0f}ms")

        return answer

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# MAIN — Compare all reranker types
